articles.title: Reply to Re: Detransitioners are “abandoned” as NHS fails to offer specialist care
articles.description: Agreement: I Agree Body: Dear Editor This article chose a particular focus: the lack of care for detransitioners, and this specific topic is signposted to the reader from the outset, in the headline and the standfirst. In the interest of balance, NHS England and the Sandyford clinic were asked for a comment but did not provide them. In response, to other specific concerns, I would make the following points: 1. Far from seeing themselves as a particular subgroup, anecdotal evidence points to detransitioners tending to regard their needs as distinct from trans patients. In many cases, they do not feel comfortable being treated in adult gender clinics. 2. The authors of this letter cite the findings of the review by Dr David Levy in his recent review of NHS adult gender dysphoria clinics (GDCs) in England. While that review did indeed reveal problems with care provision, it also identified some innovative approaches to improve access. But his review also acknowledged the lack of service provision for patients who are considering detransition and made a specific recommendation (recommendation 7) for NHS England to establish a care pathway and approach for dealing with this patient population. There is a difference between having access to a service and having no service at all; this feature was clearly focused on the latter, and it is clearly signposted as such. 3. To the point on “limited outcome measurement, quality reporting and clinical audit” making it impossible to properly understand patient outcomes and the safety of these services, more accurately Levy noted an “absence of any patient outcomes data”. His point was in relation to all patients using adult gender services, rather than just those seeking detransition care. 4. Regarding the point about coexisting conditions and broader biopsychosocial needs, nowhere does the article state that trauma, mental health difficulties and social vulnerability are “evidence that transition was inappropriate, or that gender dysphoria can be reduced to a symptom of other conditions”. 5. The co-signatories of the letter are critical of the article failing to report on extraordinary service pressures. While this is an important issue, I would argue that it more fittingly belongs to an article on systemic failings across all adult gender services. It would be relevant to include data for the number of detransitioners in the UK but, as the article points out, gender clinics don’t keep count, and 76% of detransitioners never inform the clinics that transitioned them. 6. The letter authors are critical that the feature did not include the broader social context. This is true but features have a limited word count, and information must be prioritised accordingly. 7. The authors are also critical of using individual experiences to draw broad conclusions. But while the feature begins with a compelling case study, it does not rely on lived experience to draw broad conclusions. As the article makes clear, those conclusions have already been drawn by Hilary Cass, in her 2024 seminal review of UK gender care services, which recommended that provision of care services must be made for those considering detransition. That same conclusion has also been taken up by NHS England, which has a programme of work in this field. articles.title: ‘Dhappa’: Rahul Gandhi Dodges Police, Pulls Off Akashvani Bhawan Surprise With Priyanka
articles.description: The INDIA bloc’s protest march from Parliament to the Election Commission headquarters took an unexpected turn when Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra changed course and entered the nearby Akashvani Bhawan premises. The march was planned to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. With central Delhi heavily barricaded and police and paramilitary personnel deployed, several Opposition MPs were detained and moved into buses. Rahul and Priyanka instead sat under a tree near Gate No. 4. Congress leaders later joined the protest, while some climbed the boundary wall. Congress also shared a video of the “detour” with a ‘dhappa’ caption.
